group: Historical Plains wolf (C. l. nubilus; C. variabilis Wied-Neuwied 1841)
interpretation: Authenticated Nebraska voucher SRR14761957 has a mitochondrial-only archived BAM; historical museum mtDNA does not establish a nuclear ancestry proportion, and modern Central wolves are not substituted.
The coyote-like component may be partly mediated by an older eastern-wolf lineage; it is not proof of recent direct coyote crosses.

taxonomic_scope: red wolf lineage / often C. rufus
interpretation: Large coyote-like component and private red-wolf ancestry; the percentage is conditional on a two-source model and does not settle species status.

taxonomic_scope: eastern wolf lineage / C. lycaon contested
interpretation: Ancient and more recent gene flow are plausible; a distinct eastern component prevents reading the model percentage as recent coyote hybridization.

dog_evidence: no biologically significant dog ancestry in dedicated study
interpretation: The coyote estimate is model dependent; apparent dog weight in the local three-source fit is not dog-specific and fails the direct contrast.

dog_evidence: no recent dog/coyote hybrids detected in a related Pacific Northwest sample
interpretation: The Pacific Northwest diagnostic-marker screen tests recent hybrids and does not erase the small historical genome-wide signal in a different coastal sample set.

dog_evidence: historical localized dog-derived K-locus allele documented
interpretation: Dog evidence concerns a selected coat-color haplotype rather than a measured genome-wide dog percentage.
An approximate model-based signal; population-specific dog ancestry was not established by the reviewed sources.

dog_evidence: historical localized dog-derived K-locus allele documented
interpretation: The f4-ratio is confounded by Siberian-related wolf gene flow; the dog allele is documented regionally and was not genotyped in the local Alaska genome.
The under-3-percent estimate applies to Canadian archipelago wolves in the study; small signals need cautious interpretation.
